authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of the torque produced by a force acting at a point away from the origin. Thin black axes labeled x toward the lower left, y to the right, and z upward meet at a point marked O. A heavy blue arrow labeled r, with an overhead vector arrow, runs from O down and to the right to a black dot labeled P. At P a red arrow labeled F points to the right and slightly upward, and a dashed line extends the line of r past P; the angle between that dashed extension and F is marked theta, with the same angle theta repeated on the far side of F where the dashed line of action continues to the lower right. A thin segment from near the origin meets that dashed line at a small right-angle square and is labeled r_perp. An orange arrow labeled tau rises straight up from P, standing perpendicular to the plane that holds r and F. Below and to the left, a drawn open right hand repeats the same blue r and red F arrows with curved black arrows wrapping around them to indicate the sense in which the fingers curl. Showing the geometric construction and the hand together supplies both the magnitude of the cross product, fixed by r, F, and theta, and its direction, which here lies along the positive z-axis.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for angle theta between r and F: learner rotates the force direction about point P; r_perp and the tau arrow length grow to a maximum near 90 degrees and shrink near alignment; the dependence of torque magnitude on sin(theta) becomes visible.
- Toggle between geometric construction and right-hand-rule overlay: learner switches from the r_perp/angle diagram to the hand cue; the curl direction and resulting tau arrow highlight together; the rule connecting rotation sense to torque direction becomes clear.
authoredContext:
When a force F→ is applied to a point P whose position is r→ relative to O (the figure), the torque τ→ around O is

The cross product r→×F→ also tells us the sign of the torque. In the figure, the cross product r→×F→ is along the positive z-axis, which by convention is a positive torque. If r→×F→ is along the negative z-axis, this produces a negative torque.

Now let’s consider how to define torques in the general three-dimensional case.

The torque is perpendicular to the plane defined by r→andF→ and its direction is determined by the right-hand rule.

Figure shows an XYZ coordinate system. Force F is applied in the XY plane and is parallel to the X axis. Vector r lies in the XY plane. It starts at the origin of the origin of the coordinate system and ends at the beginning of vector F. Vector for torque starts at the intersection point of r and v vectors. It is perpendicular to the XY plane and is pointed into the Z direction.

discrepancies: The source shows the right-hand illustration together with the main construction, but the generated figure hides the hand in a separate toggle mode so the full composition is never visible at once.
The initial camera/view makes the coordinate axes noticeably different: the y-axis is diagonal downward instead of the long horizontal axis to the right, reducing resemblance to the source.
The main vectors are much shorter and more compressed than in the source; r, F, and especially the orange torque vector do not match the large, prominent proportions of the textbook figure.
Vector labels render with stray square glyphs after r, F, and tau, making the labels look incorrect compared with the clean over-arrow notation in the source.
The hand overlay is a crude ellipsoid/cylinder model rather than the source's prominent illustrated hand, and it is not integrated spatially with the main diagram by default.
The lower duplicate r and F vectors with curl arrows from the source are absent in the default construction view and only partially approximated in the alternate hand mode.
evaluation.notes: The core torque construction is present and the angle slider is meaningful, but the composition, proportions, default view, integrated hand illustration, and label rendering differ substantially from the source.
action_items: Show the hand, lower r/F vectors, and curl arrows together with the geometric construction instead of hiding them in a mutually exclusive toggle.
Adjust the camera/view so z is vertical, y runs horizontally to the right, and x projects down-left as in the source.
Increase the lengths and visual prominence of r, F, and tau to match the textbook proportions.
Replace the combining-arrow labels that render as square glyphs with reliable HTML/SVG over-arrow notation or plain bold vector labels.
plan_action_items: Revise the interaction plan so the toggle does not remove source elements; it should optionally highlight or explain the right-hand rule while preserving the complete original composition.
